item.title: Monthly Summary 2026-04
item.description: The first 7 days of this month (April 1–7) saw four work streams advancing in high-intensity parallel: the TokenMonitor Linux cross-platform FloatBall bug was resolved through 10 iterations over 5 days via an architectural rewrite (fixed window + GDK Input Shape); the MIHD multimodal spatial transcriptomics paper moved from experiment wrap-up to a bilingual draft, with the discovery of the clustering-retrieval tradeoff as a core new argument; Life-Copilot completed a large-scale Discord Bot refactor (net -2,823 lines) and shipped Screen Time Tracker and other new capabilities; Gadget infrastructure completed initialization of a new Linux workstation, bidirectional data sync, and website deployment pipeline repair. The defining pattern throughout the month: low-level platform constraints (Linux GTK/WM/Wayland) repeatedly invalidated AI’s first-round assumptions, and humans drove correct fix paths by insisting on symptom description and demanding root-cause analysis; Critic subagent adversarial review proactively surfaced high-value risks — Wayland compatibility, lark-oapi blocking, and others — across multiple features.

item.title: Monthly Summary 2026-03
item.description: This month’s work was highly focused on the MIHD spatial transcriptomics multimodal clustering research project: after completing environment initialization on the DCC HPC cluster, we systematically integrated the TEDDY-G 400M foundation model, Leiden clustering algorithm, and STHD pathology annotation Ground Truth. Multi-encoder benchmarks revealed STAIG framework’s high robustness to gene encoders and the systematic transfer loss of Foundation Models on clustering tasks. The paper’s Fig 1–6 framework was finalized, marking the project’s transition from the experimental phase to the paper-writing phase.
